fn clamp(x: Int, lo: Int, hi: Int) -> Int
  requires (lo <= hi)
  ensures ((not (x < lo)) or (result == lo))
  ensures ((not (x > hi)) or (result == hi))
  ensures ((not ((x >= lo) and (x <= hi))) or (result == x))
  ensures ((result >= lo) and (result <= hi))
  effects pure
  example (clamp(5, 0, 10) == 5)
  example (clamp(-3, 0, 10) == 0)
  example (clamp(15, 0, 10) == 10)
  example (clamp(0, 0, 10) == 0)
  example (clamp(10, 0, 10) == 10)
  example (clamp(7, 7, 7) == 7)
  example (clamp(-8, -5, -2) == -5)
  example (clamp(-1, -5, -2) == -2)
{
  if (x < lo) then lo else if (x > hi) then hi else x
}

  requires (high > low)
  requires ((low * low) <= n)
  requires ((high * high) > n)

fn scan(xs: List[Int], prev: Int, current_run: Int, max_run: Int) -> Int
  requires ((current_run >= 1) and (max_run >= 1))
  ensures (result >= max_run)
  effects pure
  example (scan([], 1, 1, 1) == 1)
  example (scan([2], 1, 1, 1) == 1)
  example (scan([1, 2], 1, 1, 1) == 2)
{
  match xs { [] => if (current_run >= max_run) then current_run else max_run [h, ..t] => if (h == prev) then scan(t, h, (current_run + 1), if ((current_run + 1) >= max_run) then (current_run + 1) else max_run) else scan(t, h, 1, if (current_run >= max_run) then current_run else max_run) }
}

fn longest_run(xs: List[Int]) -> Int
  requires (len(xs) > 0)
  ensures ((result >= 1) and (result <= len(xs)))
  ensures exists i in 0..len(xs): (((i + result) <= len(xs)) and (forall j in 0..result: (xs[(i + j)] == xs[i])))
  ensures forall i in 0..len(xs): ((((i + result) + 1) > len(xs)) or (exists j in 0..(result + 1): (xs[(i + j)] != xs[i])))
  effects pure
  example (longest_run([1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3]) == 3)
  example (longest_run([7]) == 1)
  example (longest_run([1, 2, 3]) == 1)
  example (longest_run([2, 2, 2, 2]) == 4)
  example (longest_run([1, 1, 2, 1, 1, 1]) == 3)
  example (longest_run([5, 5, 6, 6]) == 2)
{
  match xs { [] => 0 [h, ..t] => scan(t, h, 1, 1) }
}

fn merge_sorted(xs: List[Int], ys: List[Int]) -> List[Int]
  requires sorted(xs)
  requires sorted(ys)
  requires forall x in xs: not contains(ys, x)
  ensures sorted(result)
  ensures (len(result) == (len(xs) + len(ys)))
  ensures forall x in xs: (count(result, x) == (count(xs, x) + count(ys, x)))
  ensures forall y in ys: (count(result, y) == (count(xs, y) + count(ys, y)))
  effects pure
  example (merge_sorted([1, 4, 9], [2, 3]) == [1, 2, 3, 4, 9])
  example (merge_sorted([], [5, 6]) == [5, 6])
  example (merge_sorted([5, 6], []) == [5, 6])
  example (merge_sorted([], []) == [])
  example (merge_sorted([1, 2, 3], [7, 8]) == [1, 2, 3, 7, 8])
  example (merge_sorted([-3, 0, 10], [-5, 4]) == [-5, -3, 0, 4, 10])
{
  match xs { [] => ys [x, ..xs_rest] => match ys { [] => xs [y, ..ys_rest] => if (x < y) then ([x] ++ merge_sorted(xs_rest, ys)) else ([y] ++ merge_sorted(xs, ys_rest)) } }
}

fn zip_sum(xs: List[Int], ys: List[Int]) -> List[Int]
  requires (len(xs) == len(ys))
  ensures (len(result) == len(xs))
  ensures forall i in 0..len(result): (result[i] == (xs[i] + ys[i]))
  effects pure
  example (zip_sum([1, 2, 3], [10, 20, 30]) == [11, 22, 33])
  example (zip_sum([], []) == [])
  example (zip_sum([5], [-5]) == [0])
{
  match xs { [] => [] [h, ..t] => match ys { [] => [] [h2, ..t2] => ([(h + h2)] ++ zip_sum(t, t2)) } }
}
